steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The Shahadah is the first and most important Pillar of Islam: "There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is his messenger." This declaration is said daily in prayer and is the only thing required to become a Muslim. | RS Exam Tips — The Five Pillars: 1. For The Five Pillars questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of The Five Pillars to its real-world impact on believers and society | UK Context: When Malcolm X converted to Islam in 1964, he recited the Shahadah to formally become a Muslim.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain why the Shahadah is the most important Pillar of Islam.

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on RS Exam Tips — The Five Pillars, UK Context, UK Context, and one past-paper question.
